card: This PR refactors PeerManagerImpl::SendMessages() in src/net_processing.cpp by extracting 17 helper functions across move-only commits, reducing the main dispatch loop from ~500 lines to under 90 lines. It addresses maintainability and review difficulty in the P2P message sending loop, an issue surfaced during review of #34824. The refactor removes redundant __func__ prefixes from debug log lines but makes no intentional behavioral changes. No dependencies are declared.
changed_since_previous: Rebased over upstream changes, incorporating the ping timeout check into the extracted timeout helpers, and added co-authorship credits.
evidence: PR description: 'PeerManagerImpl::SendMessages() is a ~500-line function handling every p2p conditional send message type inline, which makes it hard to navigate and review. This was reduced to less than 90 lines.'
Author note: Identified as an improvement while reviewing #34824 (net: encapsulate TxRelay state and replace recursive mutexes).
problem: PeerManagerImpl::SendMessages() is a monolithic ~500-line function handling all P2P message dispatching and timeout logic inline. Interleaved lock scopes and send conditions make the function difficult to navigate, analyze for thread safety, and review.

risk.why: A mistake in extracted message dispatch helpers, lock acquisitions, or timeout checks could disrupt block sync or transaction relay for connected peers.

scope_notes: All changes are in src/net_processing.cpp across 19 commits; 17 commits are pure code moves structured to be verified with git --color-moved.
summary: Extracts 17 helper functions from PeerManagerImpl::SendMessages() in src/net_processing.cpp, reducing the main P2P message dispatch function from roughly 500 lines to under 90 lines. Message generation logic, stall and timeout checks, getdata queues, and transaction trickling are separated into discrete subroutines across move-only commits. The PR also removes manual __func__ prefixes from four debug logs and standardizes helper naming and conditional formatting.
